title: MediumHello
description: `engine.hello` of the medium engine: [`EngineHello`] and the token facts of design 3.5.

baseline_available.description: A shipped baseline of exactly this Windows is in use: `baseline_trust` is `Exact`.

baseline_build.description: The local baseline's background build in this engine process.

baseline_trust.description:
How far an absence answer of the view is trusted. Below `Exact` nothing is ever offered on
absence; the view only blocks what Windows owns.

baseline_view.description:
The view in use: its name, trust and the id of the local baseline it holds. `None` when no
baseline directory is configured.

elevated.description: Whether the engine process is elevated.

shell_matches.description:
Whether the engine's token has the user and the elevation of the shell's token, so it may run a
medium-route uninstaller.

shell_sid.description: The SID of the interactive shell's account, when it is another one.

user_sid.description: The SID of the account the engine runs as.

BaselineBuild.description:
The state of the local baseline's background build (BASELINE_LOCAL_DESIGN.md §5, W4): it starts
with the engine, never blocks a scan, and a scan made before it ended can be made again after.

oneOf.description:
No build runs in this process: an exact shipped baseline, a complete cache, an engine that is
not elevated, or no cache directory. `reason` says which.
Deciding whether a build is needed.
Building. A scan made now does not use what is still being built.

scan_waiting.description:
A scan has asked for the view since the build started, so the build runs at normal
priority and that scan is worth making again when the build is done.

rescan.description: A scan ran before the build ended: making it again uses the new local baseline.

oneOf.description: The build did not produce a usable cache.

BaselineTrust.description:
How far a baseline view can be trusted when it says "this key is not Windows' own"
(BASELINE_LOCAL_DESIGN.md §4.1). Serialised by its variant name.

Presence ("Windows has it") blocks at every level. Absence is *proof* only at [`BaselineTrust::Exact`];
at `Merged` and `Local` it is *inferred* and under the trust cap (invariant L4: it never makes an item
Safe or preselected); at `None` it is never answered.

oneOf.description: A shipped baseline matches the host's (edition, build, ubr): absence is proof, as at the M1b gate.
No exact match; a complete local baseline merged with at least one shipped neighbour.
No exact match and no neighbour; a complete local baseline alone.
Anything else: absence is never answered, the scan works values-only.

BaselineViewRef.description:
The baseline view a fingerprint was harvested with (design §4.5): the trust beside the absence facts
the fingerprint stores (`ext_journal`, the subtree records).

local_id.description:
The source id of the local baseline the view held; `None` for an exact view or one without a
local baseline.

name.description: The view's name: `Professional-26340.9882` for an exact baseline, `local-…+2` for a merged one.

oneOf.description: No split token (UAC off, or not an administrator).
The elevated half of an administrator token.
The limited half of an administrator token.
